name: sensory symptoms overview
title: Numbness and tingling are localized first, central or peripheral: a thalamic lesion gives opposite-side clumsiness and burning pain, a spinal cord lesion a truncal sensory level with brisk reflexes, a root a dermatomal pattern with a lost reflex, a mononeuropathy one nerve's territory, a length-dependent polyneuropathy symmetric distal sensory loss, and Guillain-Barre syndrome weakness ascending over days with lost reflexes; each column gives what it looks like, the test that settles it and what to do

root.title: Numbness and tingling: WHERE is the lesion?
lines: characterize a neuropathy: sensory, motor or autonomic · acute (days-6 weeks), subacute (to 6 months) or chronic · its pattern · axonal or demyelinating (EMG)
pattern (root, plexus excluded): length-dependent polyneuropathy · mononeuropathy · mononeuritis multiplex
cord vs nerve, acute: a TRUNCAL SENSORY LEVEL settles it

groups.title: PERIPHERAL
lines: dorsal root ganglion · root · one nerve · many nerves

head: h
Brain: thalamus
e.g. a thalamic hemorrhage
clue: case: 78 y, LEFT thalamic bleed → right hand clumsy, right-sided burning
tx: central pain: see the NEUROPATHIC PAIN chart

head: h
Spinal cord
e.g. MS myelitis
clue: Below a level on the trunk
case: 41 y, 3 weeks: worse over 10 days, levels off, improves · 2 y ago left arm + face numb for 2 months
inv: • Babinski signs · Romberg can be positive
• case: pin level at T6, brisk legs
• stocking loss + ↓ reflexes would be SURPRISING
tx: suspect MS? brain AND spinal cord, within 6 weeks

head: h
Root (radiculopathy)
e.g. S1 after lifting
clue: case: 52 y nurse, lifted a patient · back pain down the left leg · pinprick, temperature lost on little toe + sole
tx: shooting leg pain is a root, even in a diabetic

head: h
Mononeuropathy
e.g. carpal tunnel (median nerve)
clue: case: 29 y office worker, 6 months · cousin has MS, worried

head: h
Length-dependent polyneuropathy
DIABETES: the most common cause in Canada
clue: • autonomic: postural light-headedness, urinary hesitancy, constipation
case: 78 y, type 2 diabetes · years of burning feet, poor sleep · no weakness
inv: large and small fibres · distal dying back · often painful
other causes: infection (HIV, leprosy) · drugs · metabolic (uremia, thyroid) · autoimmune · hereditary · idiopathic
tx: an analgesic or an antidepressant for neuropathic pain · best for quality of life

head: h
Guillain-Barré syndrome
acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (AIDP)
autoimmune, antibody: ANTIGEN MIMICRY after infection
clue: • toes → knees, then fingertips → legs give out
case: 26 y, cold 3 weeks ago · 3 days tingling toes, soles · weak all 4 limbs, proximal + distal
inv: • NOT muscle or cord: paresthesias + lost reflexes = NERVE
tx: • IVIG shortens the course · slow recovery, weeks to months
• can reach the cranial nerves and breathing muscles → intubation

panels.title: Nerve pathology
items: FUNCTIONAL BLOCK: reversible channel failure · lidocaine, cold, brief compression
WALLERIAN: axon breaks down distal to an injury · regrows 1-2 mm/day, months to years
DYING BACK: distal → proximal · diabetes, renal failure · vincristine, cisplatin, metronidazole · lead, arsenic, mercury, acrylamide
DEMYELINATION: GBS, CIDP, diphtheria, hereditary · remyelinates in up to 12 weeks
NEURONOPATHY: cell body · ALS, polio, West Nile · sensory: paraneoplastic, Sjögren's, B6, cisplatin

panels.title: Nerve injury after trauma
items: NEURAPRAXIA: block + demyelination, axon intact · full recovery, weeks to 3 months
AXONOTMESIS: Wallerian, Schwann cells + endoneurium kept (crush) · 3-12 months, may be incomplete
NEUROTMESIS: axon + connective tissue cut · limited regrowth · SURGICAL repair
